submission.natural_language_explanation: L16/N1688+ fires on a token that names a structured arrangement among several parts - how they are ordered, spaced, joined, split, layered, interleaved, repeated or synchronised (staggered, cascaded, nested, braided, interleaved, partitioned, layered, blended, composite, alternating, modular, hierarchical, sorted, orthogonal, woven, shuffled). The word itself carries the signal - it fires just as hard whatever head noun follows, and quietens only when the same word is pushed out of premodifier position - and it stays at zero on ordinary descriptive, evaluative and domain-classifying adjectives and on the head nouns themselves; the 552-token scan only caught the pole's saturated double-negative SwiGLU regime (g<0 and u<0, peaks at or below 0.67), so the scan's function-word and digit peaks belong to that regime rather than to this feature.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Brother Anselm arrived at the abbey of Saint Gall in the autumn of the year the river froze early, carrying a single satchel and a letter of introduction that the porter read twice before admitting him. The letter said little beyond his name and the house that had sent him, and the porter, who had admitted many men with better letters and worse intentions, waved him through the gate without comment. Anselm had walked nine days to get there and had expected some ceremony; what he got was a nod and a direction to the kitchen.

Beyond the gate lay a courtyard of packed earth, swept clean despite the season, and beyond that a long low building whose roof sagged in the middle like a tired animal. He would learn later that the roof had sagged for eighty years and that three successive abbots had promised to repair it and had each found a more urgent use for the money. He would learn a great many things in the slow way that monasteries teach, by standing in the right room at the wrong hour until someone explained the obvious.

The first winter was the hardest. The dormitory was cold in a way that seemed personal, and the rule of silence meant his complaints stayed inside his own skull, where they grew louder instead of quieter. He learned to sleep with his hands under his arms and to wake before the bell so that the shock of it would not be the first thing he felt. He learned the names of the brothers by their seats at table: the seat came from seniority, and seniority came from the year a man had arrived, and that was the only history that mattered inside the walls. He learned, too, that the bell was rung by a different brother each week, that the ringing was always a little wrong, and that no one minded.

By the second spring the abbot had assigned him to the scriptorium, and there Anselm found the work that would occupy eleven years of his life. The room ran the length of the east wing and its windows faced the morning, because ink dries slowly in cold air and the copyists needed every hour of light they could get. Twelve desks stood in two rows. The men at them worked with their heads down and their sleeves pinned back, and the only sounds were the scrape of pens and the occasional cough that could not be helped.

For the first year he was given only the parts of books that no one would read: tables of chapters, lists of feast days, the long columns of names that begin a martyrology. He came to love the columns. They were dull and they were safe, and a mistake in a column of names was a mistake that Gervase could correct in the margin without embarrassment to anyone. He learned the shape of letters by copying the same letters ten thousand times, and he learned patience the way a stone learns water. Some afternoons Gervase would take the sheet away and bring it back with a single mark beside the worst mistake, and that one mark taught him more than a page of instruction.

The scriptorium was run along strictly hierarchical lines, though no one ever said so aloud: the master of copyists sat nearest the windows with the best light and the warmest corner, then the two brothers who had copied the most volumes, then the men who had copied fewer, and finally the novices at the dark end by the door, where the draught made the ink skin over and the work went slowly. A brother's seat moved forward only when another seat emptied, and seats emptied mostly when men died, so the room changed shape roughly once a generation and otherwise held its own.

Anselm died at the abbey in the winter of his sixty-third year, having risen to the seat by the second window. The men who buried him could not have said what he had copied, only that he had copied it cleanly, and the psalters he made were still in use a century later, when the roof finally fell in and the abbot, the fourth one, at last found the money to repair it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis says the word itself carries the signal wherever it occurs in premodifier position, so 'hierarchical', a single model token, deep inside a long narrative passage from a genre unlike the examples should still fire on that token.
